newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra to review Australian pay TV content.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra to review Australian pay TV content.

text.p: Australian Communications Minister Richard Alston announced on Thursday the details of a review into Australian content on pay television.

"The government is determined that Australian content be given every opportunity to compete with overseas programming for a place on our broadcasting services, particularly pay TV," Alston said in a statement.
The review would examine the nature of pay TV's contribution to Australia's cultural identity, Alston said.
The review would also examine how appropriate it was to apply local content regulations to channels other than designated drama channels, Alston said in a statement.

Each drama pay TV service is currently subject to a licence condition, under which at least 10 percent of its annual programme spending is allocated to new Australian drama programmes. Alston said the review would examine the feasibility of lifting this requirement to 20 percent.
In addition, the review would consider the changing environment for pay TV, particularly lifting restrictions relating to advertising and satellite licences in mid-1997.
"I have asked the Australian Broadcasting Authority to make a substantial contribution to the review, in light of its experience in the administration of the current licence condition," Alston said.
The review is scheduled to be completed by July 1 next year.
Australia's main pay TV operators are Foxtel, a joint venture owned by News Corp Ltd and telecommunications giant Telstra Corp, and Optus Vision.

Optus Vision is owned 46.5 percent by Australian telecommunications carrier Optus Communications and U.S. based Continental CableVision Inc, which has merged with U.S. West . The remainder is owned by the Seven Network Ltd and Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd.
Australis Media Ltd also operates in the microwave and satellite pay TV market.
